source: Technology Promotion Project to Increase Productivity Around Tonle Sap (TSTD — TA 7305-CAM), watermelon (ដំណាំឪឡឹក) technical training booklet, prepared by the project's agricultural techniques and extension officer in cooperation with East West Seed International, November 2016. Contact: livleanghy@gmail.com
text:
Water watermelon in the morning by letting water flow into the furrows/channels between the planting beds. Watering at midday or in the late afternoon/evening is discouraged, as it can encourage disease and stress the plants.

Watering needs to be given regularly and consistently — neither letting the crop run short of water nor over-watering, since either extreme can damage the plants and increase disease pressure. Uneven or inconsistent watering can also lead to poor fruit development.

A simple soil-moisture check is recommended: if the soil around the base of the plant is loose and dry (crumbles and will not hold together when squeezed), additional watering is needed; if the soil there is already sticky/compacted and holds together, no extra watering is needed at that time. Fertilizer application should also be timed to help the plant develop and mature quickly.
